question: Should QQBot permanently reject inbound gateway messages above 1 MiB, or should this channel use a larger ceiling until production event-size limits are established?
rationale: The dependency mechanism is correct, but neither the official QQ documentation nor authenticated production evidence defines the largest legitimate gateway event, so automation cannot safely choose the compatibility/security tradeoff.

options.title: Approve 1 MiB after owner validation
options.body: Confirm that legitimate QQ gateway events remain below 1 MiB, then rebase and preserve the merged handshake timeout alongside this cap.

options.title: Use a larger defensive ceiling
options.body: Select a more compatibility-tolerant bound such as 16 MiB while still eliminating the dependency's 100 MiB default window.

options.title: Pause pending platform evidence
options.body: Keep the dependency default until authenticated traffic evidence or a platform contract supports a permanent channel-specific ceiling.

recommendation.title: Approve 1 MiB after owner validation
recommendation.body: Confirm that legitimate QQ gateway events remain below 1 MiB, then rebase and preserve the merged handshake timeout alongside this cap.

likelyOwner.reason: Their feature history is the strongest available signal for ownership of QQBot gateway architecture and its transport constraints.
